_comment: Drives the npx installer. Each entry copies a source dir from the repo (at the pinned ref) into the consuming repo. 'kind' selects the per-agent emitter (skill|kit|rule|agent). 'to' is the Claude destination; other agents' destinations are derived from kind. 'wire: true' = one-time manual setup needed (the installer prints a note, never auto-merges build config).

shared.wire: Merge justfile.snippet into your root justfile and set the *_dir variables to your layout — this is the ONE place paths live. It defines `just check` + per-tech recipes (rust-lint/rust-check, ts-*, go-*) that both the git hooks and the agent call. autonomy.md auto-loads from .claude/rules/agent/ (no wiring). (`claude-rules init` can assemble this for you.) adr-check.mjs is OPT-IN: move it to scripts/ and add `adr-check` to the `check` recipe if the repo keeps ADRs under docs/adr/ (see rules/agent/decisions.md). docs-check.mjs is OPT-IN the same way (`docs-check`), for a repo with a PRD/PLAN under docs/ — it fails on an index and its units disagreeing, warns on the budgets, `--strict` to enforce them (see rules/product/documents.md, shipped with the `product` profile). Both gates read their budgets from `.docs-budgets.json` at the repo root (e.g. `{ "prd": { "indexCeiling": 1500 }, "adr": { "unitCeiling": 900 } }`) — put a repo-specific threshold THERE, not in the script: the installer never writes that file, so `update` cannot reset it. The snippet also carries the Tier 3 recipes (`mutate-diff` → rust-mutate/ts-mutate/go-cover): mutation on the merge-base diff, run per coherent block BEFORE the push, never in a hook and never in `check` — uncomment the techs whose tool you installed, set `base` if your trunk is not origin/main, and gitignore pr.diff/coverage.out. `dup-check` (jscpd via npx, no install) is opt-in too: baseline the number before adding it to `check`.

rust.wire: Merge lefthook.snippet.yml into lefthook.yml (thin triggers → `just rust-lint`/`rust-check`) and set `rust_dir` in the justfile. Move deny.toml→<rust_dir>, mutants.toml→<rust_dir>/.cargo/, mutation-ci.yaml→.gitea/workflows/ (set its working-directory to your rust_dir). Tier 3 also runs LOCALLY: `cargo install cargo-mutants` and uncomment `rust-mutate` in the justfile's `mutate-diff` — the CI job is the witness, not the first observation. rust-fmt.sh is a SPECIAL CASE (generated member crate): swap the fmt command in rust-check + add #![allow(clippy::all)] to that crate. See .claude/kit/README.md.

ts._note: TS language baseline: quality-gate rules + the kit gates. React frontend architecture lives in the `portal-flat` profile; a Node/TS backend adds `api` + `backend`.
ts.wire: Merge lefthook.snippet.yml into lefthook.yml (thin triggers → `just ts-lint`/`ts-check`) and set `ts_dir` in the justfile. Adapt eslint.config.base.js globalIgnores into your eslint config. Tier 3 (optional): move mutation-ci.yaml→.gitea/workflows/ (or .github/workflows/), `npm i -D @stryker-mutator/core` + a runner, `npx stryker init` — then uncomment `ts-mutate` in the justfile's `mutate-diff` to run it locally before pushing (Stryker has no `--since`, so local uses `--incremental`; gitignore reports/). See rules/testing/ratchet.md for the calibrate-then-ratchet sequence.

go.wire: Merge lefthook.snippet.yml into lefthook.yml (thin triggers → `just go-lint`/`go-check`) and set `go_dir` in the justfile. Move golangci.base.yml→<go_dir>/.golangci.yml. Tier 3 (optional): move coverage-ci.yaml→.gitea/workflows/ (or .github/workflows/) and commit a `.coverage-baseline` next to the module — Go has no production-grade mutation tool, so this is a coverage ratchet (the weaker signal; the file's header says why). Locally, uncomment `go-cover` in the justfile's `mutate-diff`: it prints the map of uncovered statements, which is the part worth reading before a push (the numeric ratchet stays in CI).

godot._note: Godot 4 + C# (strong typing) game profile — gate: gamedev. Co-location by entity, composition over inheritance, single typed EventBus, all gameplay data in .tres (zero hardcoded values), legacy .gd migration policy (no new .gd). Path-scoped **/*.cs (+ .tscn/.tres/.gd where relevant).

godot.wire: Merge lefthook.snippet.yml into lefthook.yml (thin triggers → `just godot-lint`/`godot-check`) and justfile.snippet into the justfile; set godot_dir/godot_bin/godot_export_preset. chmod +x check-no-new-gd.sh. Godot project needs C# (.NET) + export templates + GDUnit4 + a matching export preset. Ships Roslyn analyzers (GODOT001 hardcoded values, GODOT002 signal placement, GODOT003 string node paths) that run inside dotnet build — reference the analyzer .csproj from the game project. The headless-export gate catches broken .tscn/.tres refs the C# compiler can't. See kit/godot/README.md.

hexagonal._note: Architecture pattern — gate: backend/fullstack. Ships the agnostic principle + language idioms (rust/go), path-scoped so only your language's loads. `rust-add-domain` is the rust DI-container transformation skill (needs rust-di-container.md). `architect` recommends this for backend/fullstack shapes.

cqrs._note: Architecture pattern — gate: EXPLICIT opt-in only (non-standard). The rust variant assumes the home library `cqrs-rust-lib` (github.com/dohrm/cqrs-rust-lib). Add explicitly: `add cqrs`.

portal-flat._note: React framework quality gates (Rules of Hooks, purity, RTL, a11y) — decoupled from the flat-domain architecture, applies to any React app.

Frontend architecture — gate: frontend. Flat-domain modular React portal: agnostic principle + React idioms (OpenAPI-generated client, TanStack Query, contexts). Leptos support was dropped. Pairs with `ts` (language baseline).

portal-flat.wire: Copy openapi-ts.config.ts to your frontend root. Install: `npm i -D @hey-api/openapi-ts` + `npm i @hey-api/client-axios @tanstack/react-query zod`. Add package.json scripts `generate:api` ("openapi-ts", live backend) and `generate:api:file` (same, CI sets OPENAPI_SPEC to the spec artifact). Create src/config/hey-api.ts exporting the client runtimeConfig (base URL + auth interceptor). Ensure eslint globalIgnores and tsconfig exclude src/api/generated. NOT a hook tier — codegen is a dev/CI step, not a gate.

testing._note: Cross-language test doctrine — gate: any repo that has tests (so: always, once code exists). strategy (levels, determinism, flaky policy), contract (the OpenAPI spec as the gated contract between `api` and `portal-flat`, plus events/DB/third parties), ratchet (coverage is a symptom, mutation is the gate, baseline→observe→ratchet). Path-scoped rs/go/ts/tsx. The executable Tier-3 counterparts ship with the language kits: kit/rust/mutation-ci.yaml, kit/ts/mutation-ci.yaml, kit/go/coverage-ci.yaml.

cicd._note: Delivery pipeline doctrine — gate: any repo with a forge. pipeline (CI calls `just check` and never reimplements it; tiers→jobs; pinning, caching, least privilege, no skip-as-pass) + release (the tag is a human act, SemVer on the contract, changelog for consumers, immutable tags). Path-scoped to workflow files + CHANGELOG.md, so it loads when you touch the pipeline, not every session.

cicd.wire: Copy ci.snippet.yaml → .github/workflows/ci.yaml (or .gitea/workflows/), DELETE the jobs for technologies you don't have, and set `runs-on` to your runner label (GitHub: ubuntu-latest; Gitea: often `linux`). Same for release.snippet.yaml if the repo publishes anything — adapt the manifest read + the build/publish steps. Then make the `ci-ok` job the ONE required check in branch protection. `just` must be on the runner (bake it into the image, or keep the pinned install step). `/ci-setup` does all of this for you and prints what's left.

cicd._note: Bootstraps or audits the pipeline from what is actually installed (lock + justfile + existing workflows). Its audit mode produces the drift table: any CI command that is not a justfile recipe is drift the agent's local loop cannot see.

ops._note: Run-time doctrine, platform-agnostic — gate: any service that runs somewhere (backend/fullstack). observability (three signals, cardinality is the bill, the minimum set, OTLP out and no vendor SDK in domain code), slo (good/valid ratios measured where the user is, error budget with a consequence, burn-rate alerts, no alert without a runbook), delivery (deploy ≠ release, expand/backfill/migrate/contract, rehearsed rollback, flags as dated debt). Language rules own HOW to log; these own WHAT to emit and what is promised. Add `k8s` on top when it deploys to Kubernetes.

Turns the PRD's success criteria into 1-3 computable SLIs, proposes targets as ADRs, audits the code for instrumentation gaps and cardinality bombs, and produces the burn-rate alert table (owner + runbook + action per row). Writes docs/OBSERVABILITY.md.

incident._note: One runbook per failure mode, written for a responder who was asleep four minutes ago: mitigate before diagnosing, every step a command harvested from the repo (justfile, manifests, CLI — never invented), each check stating what a good and a bad answer mean, plus the destructive moves that look like progress. Rehearsed or marked Unrehearsed. Required by ops/slo.md; called by /observability when it builds the alert table.

Retrospective mirror of /pre-mortem. Blameless, no single root cause, timeline from evidence, and detect/mitigate/resolve reported separately because they lead to different work. Action items are system changes classed prevent/detect/mitigate with an owner and a date; everything touching another document is a hand-off delta (it owns docs/postmortem/ and nothing else).

k8s._note: The manifest layer that makes the `ops` rules true on Kubernetes, and corrects the defaults that are actively wrong: memory limit = request but a CPU limit usually harmful, liveness never on a dependency, terminationGracePeriod > drain timeout + a preStop sleep (the 503s of a 'zero-downtime' rollout), maxUnavailable 0 with a PDB, migrations as a Job before the rollout, pod-template checksum on config change, bounded Jobs. Path-scoped to manifest/chart directories. Install with `ops`.

tauri._note: Tauri v2 desktop app — gate: EXPLICIT opt-in. Extends `portal-flat` with the IPC transport (invoke/listen, no HTTP, no OpenAPI, no TanStack Query — Zustand stores instead). Install alongside `ts portal-flat rust`.

api._note: Opinionated HTTP-API stack — gate: backend/fullstack. rust=axum+utoipa, go=chi+Huma, node=Fastify. All emit OpenAPI (the contract `portal-flat` generates its client from). Path-scoped per language; add explicitly: `add api`.

backend._note: Cross-language backend conventions — gate: backend/fullstack. Error contract (problem+json), config & secrets, health & lifecycle, pagination. Language-agnostic; add explicitly: `add backend`.

investigate._note: Opt-in, language-agnostic skill — a 4-phase debug methodology (locate → hypothesize → instrument → fix), model-independent. Add explicitly: `add investigate`.

loop-setup._note: Opt-in, language- and host-agnostic skill — frames a self-terminating agent loop (4 preconditions → bounded objective → measurable done-command → budget/iteration guardrails) and writes PLAN.md + MEMORY.md + the loop prompt. Handoff branches per host: Claude /loop, Codex /goal, Cursor automation. Named loop-setup to avoid collision with Claude's built-in /loop. Add explicitly: `add loop-setup`.

product._note: The one convention behind the product skills: a document that must GROW is a directory of append-only units plus a compacted index (the shape `docs/adr/` already has), never one file that gets longer. Carries the per-document split thresholds (plan → phase units, PRD → capability units), the unit/index budgets, the freeze-on-shipped rule, and the one-home-per-fact routing table. Path-scoped to `docs/**/*.md`, so it loads when the agent touches the documents it governs. /prd, /plan and /architect defer to it rather than restating the budgets.

Opt-in product-lifecycle skills. Chain: interview → prd (what) → architect (how/ADRs) + design-system (visual) + experience (behavior: DX / web UX / CLI-TUI UX) → plan (phases); diagram supports throughout. design-system and experience are complementary — the former owns visual tokens (docs/DESIGN.md), the latter owns flows/states/feedback/a11y (docs/EXPERIENCE.md) and consumes the former's tokens. ui-prompt is a downstream export that reads BOTH docs and composes a ready-to-paste prompt for a UI generator (Artifacts/v0/Lovable/Bolt…), scoped to one screen — web UI only, agnostic to the target tool. pre-mortem is an adversarial risk gate downstream of prd/architect that loops back into them via hand-off deltas (it owns docs/premortem/<target>-<horizon>.md — one register per exercise — never edits PRD/ADR/PLAN). Adapted from claude-mastery + `architect`, `experience` and `pre-mortem` added here. Dependency-free, brand-neutral. Git-flow commands (branche/livre) intentionally dropped. Add explicitly: `add product`.
